subject: Throughput sizing \u000B post-call SLOs & next steps
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood - throughput sizing call

Thanks again for the call earlier today, Rafael - that was helpful. A couple quick clarifications for our execs so we can align internally before the follow-up:

- We want to confirm the latency SLO targets you heard us state: 95th percentile end-to-end <= 300ms for responses up to ~512 output tokens, and start-of-stream (first byte) <= 150ms for streaming use-cases. Is that in scope?
- For throughput: I think we said steady-state QPS is ~40 req/s, average request ~250 tokens (input+output), and peak burst up to ~250 req/s for ~2 minutes during market open. Can you validate those numbers sound right for sizing?

Also attaching the two slides our CTO wanted you to see (we'll send the sample prompt histogram after we clean PII). Next steps for us: a short follow-up to get a sizing proposal and a rough price ballpark.

Thanks,
Samir
VP Product, FinEx

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood - throughput sizing call (post-call recap & ask)

Samir - really appreciate the clear readout. Quick post-call recap and initial sizing assumptions so we can align the follow-up:

Recap (as I captured it):
- Latency SLOs: 95th <= 300ms end-to-end for responses up to ~512 tokens (chat), start-of-stream <= 150ms for streaming-first-byte.
- Steady-state: ~40 QPS (requests/s).
- Peak bursts: up to ~250 QPS sustained for ~2 minutes (market open); other peaks up to ~60 QPS for ~15 minutes.
- Average payload: ~250 tokens total (input + output); typical higher-value flows ~500 tokens.
- Concurrency: observed ~150 concurrent active requests during peak.

Initial sizing notes / what we'll validate next:
- Tokens/sec: using 250 tokens/req -> steady ~10k tokens/sec, peak ~62.5k tokens/sec.
- Important to understand distribution: if a meaningful % of requests are streaming (long-running responses with early-first-byte) we tune for lower first-byte latency (smaller batch windows) versus pure throughput.
- KV cache / prefix caching could reduce backend compute for repeat prompts; if you have hot prompts we should get hit-rate estimates.

Action items for us (what I'll do with Marissa and Neha):
1) Run a quick back-of-envelope capacity calc and attach it (see throughput_estimate.xlsx & redwood_sizing_calc.csv).
2) Propose a recommended test plan (synthetic load + a brief canary with real traffic).
3) Provide a ballpark committed-capacity recommendation (Dedicated pool sizing) and a rough cost estimate to cover steady + burst handling with automatic overflow/fallback options.

Questions for you:
- Can you confirm the 2-minute burst duration and the worst-case request token sizes (we need 95th and max token counts)?
- Do you expect most traffic to be streaming chat or single-shot completion calls?
- Will you be able to share a sanitized sample of request/response token sizes or a histogram? Even 500 rows is super helpful.

Marissa / Neha - looping you in for the sizing call out. Marissa can run a synthetic load and Neha can advise on kernel/quantization tradeoffs for long sequences.

Samir - if the recap above looks right I'll turn this into a short proposal + recommended next-call agenda (30m) - propose Wed 2027-02-09 09:00 PT unless you prefer another time.

Thanks,
Rafael
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@finex.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood - throughput sizing call (synthetic test + notes)

Adding a quick engineering note from my side:

- For the numbers Rafael laid out, the key trade is batch size vs first-byte latency. For streaming-first-byte <=150ms I'd plan for smaller batch windows (~5-20ms) which increases GPU utilization overhead; we'll quantify in the sizing calc.
- If ~30-40% of requests are long (>512 tokens) you'll want to explore quantized model variants (we can test 4-bit Q8 modes) to reduce baseline cost. Neha - can you confirm approximate GPU count estimate for steady + burst? I'll update the spreadsheet once we have the sanitized token histogram.
- I can run a synthetic load profile that simulates your steady + 2-minute burst and report observed latencies (first-byte and completion). If Samir can share an example prompt or the histogram sample, that will make the test representative.

Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood - throughput sizing call

Thanks Rafael / Marissa - this matches our notes. A few answers:

- Confirm the 2-minute burst at market open is the material one; we see the ~250 QPS spike there and smaller micro-bursts later in the day.
- We ran a quick export and sanitized a histogram: 75th percentile request size ~180 tokens, 95th ~420 tokens, max ~1024 tokens. I'll upload a sanitized CSV (no PII) to the Drive link and cc you when it's available - target <24 hours.
- Traffic mix: roughly 70% single-shot completions, 30% streaming chat.

Can you include in the proposal a ballpark monthly cost range for: 1) hosted API + autoscaling to cover peak, and 2) dedicated reserved pool sized to handle steady + managed overflow? Also please include suggested SLA/rollout approach for the canary.

Samir

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood - throughput sizing call (proposal & next steps)

Perfect - thanks for the histogram ETA, Samir. Next steps from Redwood:

1) I'll convert today's notes into a short proposal that includes:
   - Sizing assumptions (we'll use the 95th token sizes you provided: 420 tokens)
   - Back-of-envelope GPU / capacity estimate to meet your 95th-latency SLO with the streaming-first-byte constraint
   - Two cost scenarios: hosted autoscale (on-demand) and Dedicated reserved pool with overflow fallback.

2) Marissa will run a synthetic load test (steady 40 QPS + a 2-minute 250 QPS burst) once we have the sanitized histogram. Expect a short report within 48 hours of receiving the sample.

3) Neha will validate model variant/quantization options for long-sequence requests and provide recommended configs for the canary.

4) Proposed follow-up demo & sizing review (30m): Wed 2027-02-09 09:00 PT - please confirm or propose another slot.

Samir - we'll include a ballpark monthly cost range in the proposal; it will be a wide band until we validate with the synthetic run and can decide on quantized variants.

If that aligns, I'll send the proposal + calendar invite and attach the sizing spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Rafael
